title: Sky received 70% of GROVE's genesis supply, giving the parent ecosystem majority ownership of its Agent's token
content:
The distribution chain in A.6.1.1.2.2.1.4.2.1.2 through A.6.1.1.2.2.1.4.2.1.2.3.2 is structurally revealing regardless of the exact figures. The Genesis Supply was minted to a **Grove Foundation** account, not to Grove's onchain SubProxy. From there, 7 billion of the 10 billion supply went to the **Sky Pause Proxy**, and 3 billion to the Grove SubProxy, which then pushed the majority of its share out to the Grove Labs Multisig and a smaller allocation to the Grove Foundation Multisig.

Two design choices are embedded here. First, **the parent owns the child**: Sky holds the supermajority of the Agent's token from inception, so the Agent's equity upside accrues mostly to Sky rather than to the Agent's own operators. This is what makes an Agent a growth vehicle for Sky rather than a competitor for capital.

Second, **the Foundation is the mint origin**, not the protocol. The token comes into existence in a legal entity's hands and is distributed outward by transfer. That places the initial allocation under off-chain fiduciary control and makes the transfers themselves auditable historical facts recorded in the Artifact.

The residual Agent-side allocation sitting in the Grove Labs Multisig is the contributor-incentive pool; the split between it and the Foundation multisig determines whether operator incentives or institutional reserves dominate Grove's own stake.
description: The Grove Foundation minted the entire supply, then transferred 7 billion to the Sky Pause Proxy; of Grove's own 3 billion, the bulk went to Grove Labs and a slice to the Foundation multisig.
